landmarks.name: Kuwait Towers
landmarks.writeup: Iconic water towers and a symbol of modern Kuwait, featuring observation decks with panoramic views.

landmarks.name: Grand Mosque
landmarks.writeup: The largest mosque in Kuwait, known for its impressive Islamic architecture and cultural significance.

landmarks.name: Al Shaheed Park
landmarks.writeup: A large urban park featuring museums, green spaces, and memorials dedicated to Kuwait's martyrs.

landmarks.name: Liberation Tower
landmarks.writeup: One of the tallest telecommunications towers in the world, symbolizing Kuwait's liberation.

head_of_state: His Highness Sheikh Nawaf Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah (Emir)

cultural_events.name: Hala February Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Annual festival celebrating Kuwait's liberation with cultural shows, parades, and traditional activities.

cultural_events.name: Kuwait International Book Fair
cultural_events.writeup: A major cultural event promoting literature and education with participation from international publishers.

food_writeup: Kuwaiti cuisine features rich, flavorful dishes often centered around rice, meat, and seafood, with popular dishes like machboos (spiced rice with meat) and mutabbaq samak (fish with rice).
brief_history: Kuwait emerged as a trading hub in the 18th century, became a British protectorate in the early 20th century, gained independence in 1961, and was liberated from Iraqi occupation in 1991.

important_people.name: Sheikh Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah
important_people.description: Former Emir and key figure in Kuwait's development

current_conflicts: Kuwait is currently stable with no active internal or external conflicts, focusing on regional diplomacy and economic development.
